title: cloneOrPull uses name-only matching — could misidentify repos with identical names
description: Verified: src/index.ts:88 — `const isCloned = existing.has(repo.name) && fs.existsSync(path.join(repoPath, '.git'))`. If two different GitHub repos have the same name (e.g., forked repos from different owners), the tool will treat the existing directory as the same repo and attempt `git pull` instead of cloning the new repo. This is a rare edge case (requires starring two repos with identical names from different owners) but would result in incorrect sync behavior.
spec:
1. After confirming isCloned, add a remote URL check: read the current remote origin URL from the existing repo via `git -C {repoPath} config --get remote.origin.url` and compare it to `repo.clone_url`.
2. If the URLs don't match, treat it as a new clone (remove or rename the existing directory first, or skip with a warning).
